newsitem.title: TURKEY: Goldman Sachs named Turk Telekom selloff adviser.
newsitem.headline: Goldman Sachs named Turk Telekom selloff adviser.

text.p: Turkey has appointed a consortium headed by Goldman Sachs to advise it on the stalled sale of Turk Telekom, the lynchpin of the government's privatisation programme, State Minister Ufuk Soylemez said on Wednesday.
"The consortium has been chosen in accordance with the Telekom law and World Bank standards. Advisory services will be supplied by the consortium led by Goldman Sachs," he told reporters.
He said he hoped 10-15 percent of Telekom would be ready for offer in up to three months after Goldman Sachs had completed its advisory services and the sale strategy had been worked out.

The government hopes to raise $3.5 billion from the sale, previously hindered by constitutional challenges. Parliament in August amended a privatisation bill that will ease the sale, but it was again challenged by opposition MPs.
The constitutional court began debating in late November an application for the cancellation of the sell-off law currently in effect. It is not known when it will rule.
Goldman Sachs beat off bids from four other consortia, led by Lehman Brothers, Morgan Stanley, N.M. Rothschild and Salomon Brothers.
